findings.title: PR authors can bypass the ticket gate
findings.description: The `ticket-link` job checks out the pull request’s merge revision and runs `scripts/pr-ticket-check.ts` from that revision as its required validator. A contributor can change the script or workflow in their pull request to return success despite a missing issue link or backlog update, while retaining the `ticket-link` check name.

findings.title: Failing checks do not block merges
findings.description: The new workflows define check contexts, but neither workflow configuration nor the documented process enables branch protection that requires those contexts on `main`. With the repository’s documented absence of branch protection, a pull request can be merged while either platform check or `ticket-link` is red or missing.

findings.title: Script output and exit code are set outside src/cli.ts
findings.description: The new `scripts/pr-ticket-check.ts` writes to `process.stdout` and `process.stderr` and sets `process.exitCode` in its entry block, which the rule reserves for `src/cli.ts`. The same pattern appears in the new `scripts/ticket-ready.ts` (its entry block writes both streams and sets `process.exitCode`), so the rule is departed from in two files. The author's notes say the human will decide whether the convention is scoped to `src/`, but the rule as written names no exception, so the code departs from it until that decision is made. Any later change to the entry block also has to be checked by hand against this rule.

findings.title: Backlog edits can break both test jobs
findings.description: The new `pr-ticket-check` tests read the repository’s live `BACKLOG.md` and assert its current T-001 and T-007 status strings rather than using a fixed fixture. A later, valid backlog cleanup changes those unrelated strings and fails `npm test`, which the new Linux and Windows check jobs both run.

findings.title: An edited ticket can pass on stale text
findings.description: The investigation step passes `github.event.issue.body` from the `labeled` event to `ticket-ready.ts`, without checking the current issue body. If the issue is edited after labeling but before the queued job runs, the guard can approve a removed investigation or reject one added before execution, while the agent reads the current ticket.

findings.title: Ticket results can reflect the wrong tree
findings.description: The `ticket-link` checkout has no explicit head ref, so `run` reads `BACKLOG.md` from the pull request’s synthetic merge commit rather than the head commit specified by its input contract. If the base branch changes that row before a queued or rerun check executes, the result can reflect content absent from the submitted head or reject a head that contains the expected row.

findings.title: Guard failures blame a valid ticket
findings.description: The workflow treats every nonzero result from `node scripts/ticket-ready.ts` as an empty or missing Investigation section. If Node cannot load the script or the guard crashes, the step removes `ready-for-agent` and tells the human to edit the ticket instead of identifying the tooling failure.

findings.title: Script output bypasses the cli-only rule
findings.description: The entry blocks of `scripts/pr-ticket-check.ts` and `scripts/ticket-ready.ts` call `process.stdout.write`, `process.stderr.write` and set `process.exitCode`. The checklist allows these only in `src/cli.ts`, so the literal rule is breached in two files. The author reports that the human chose to amend the rule in AGENTS.md to allow entry blocks under `scripts/`, but the checklist text still forbids it, so the same wording will flag every factory script that follows the amended convention until the rule is re-imported.

findings.title: A one-line triple-backtick span hides the rest of a ticket
findings.description: `FENCE_OPEN` (`^ {0,3}(`{3,}|~{3,})`) treats any line that starts with three backticks as an opening fence, even one like "```npm test``` passes". CommonMark does not count that as a fence, because a backtick fence's info string cannot contain backticks. Because the fence never closes, `visibleLines` blanks every later line, so `hasInvestigation` turns away a ticket whose Investigation section comes after such a line, even though GitHub shows it.

findings.title: Investigations written with sub-headings are refused
findings.description: In `hasInvestigation`, `NEXT_SECTION` treats deeper Markdown headings and lines beginning with a bold phrase ending in a period as section boundaries, stopping before it reads their content. When `## Investigation` begins with a subheading such as `### What was checked`, or its prose begins with `**Checked.**`, the guard can return false, causing the label workflow to remove `ready-for-agent` and post a misleading rejection.

findings.title: Titles naming an earlier ticket stay red
findings.description: `checkPrTicket` treats every T-NNN in the PR title as a ticket the PR finishes, and requires the BACKLOG row for each one to say `done (PR <this number>)`. A title such as `feat(config): custom section names (T-027, split from T-008)`, written the same way as the existing T-027 backlog row, cannot pass unless the author overwrites T-008's history row `done (PR 21)`.
